01020304050607
ABOUT THIS REPORT
Reporting Scope and Boundary
This  IAR  2025  covers  the  period  from  1  July  
2024 to 30 June 2025, unless stated otherwise. 
It encompasses the core operational activities of 
KIP  REIT.  All  data,  information  and  disclosures  
included  in  IAR  2025  are  limited  to  business  
entities, assets, and operations that fall under the 
full operational control of KIP REIT.
Reporting Frameworks and Standards
• Main Market Listing Requirements ("MMLR") 
of Bursa Malaysia Securities Berhad (“Bursa 
Securities”)
• Companies Act 2016 (“CA 2016”)
• Malaysian Code on Corporate Governance 
("MCCG")
•   Malaysian   Financial   Reporting   Standards   
("MFRS")     and     International     Financial     
Reporting Standards ("IFRS")
•   Securities   Commission   ("SC")   Malaysia's   
Guidelines on Listed Real Estate Investment 
Trusts ("REITs")
•    FTSE4Good    Bursa    Malaysia    ("F4GBM")    
Index
•  Bursa  Securities'  Sustainability  Reporting  
Guide (3rd edition)
• Global Reporting Initiative (“GRI”) Standards 
- With reference
• IIRC's Integrated Reporting Framework
•  Task  Force  on  Climate-Related  Financial  
Disclosures ("TCFD")
•  United  Nations  Sustainable  Development  
Goals ("UN SDGs")
Assurance
Contents  of  this  report  have  been  read  and  
approved by the Board of Directors ("the Board") 
of KIP REIT Management Sdn Bhd ("the Manager")  
and   Management.   The   financial   statements   
included  in  this  IAR  have  been  independently  
audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers PLT (“PwC”). 
As  part  of  the  Manager’s  continuous  efforts  to  
enhance  KIP  REIT’s  sustainability  reporting,  the  
Manager has also appointed Deloitte PLT to carry 
out  an  independent  limited  assurance  exercise  
on   selected   indicators   in   the   Sustainability   
Statement. 
KIP  Real  Estate  Investment  Trust  (“KIP  REIT”)  is  pleased  to  
present   its   Integrated   Annual   Report   2025   (“IAR   2025”)   
for  the  financial  year  ended  30  June  2025  (“FYE  2025”).  
This  report  outlines  KIP  REIT’s  financial  and  non-financial  
performance and has been prepared in accordance with the 
Guiding Principles and Content Elements of the International 
Integrated  Reporting  Framework  issued  by  the  International  
Integrated Reporting Council (“IIRC”).

OVERVIEW
Materiality
Information  disclosed  in  this  IAR  2025  is  
relevant  to  KIP  REIT’s  material  matters,  
which     have     been     determined     by     
extensive   stakeholder   engagement   as   
well as internal evaluation. These material 
matters reflect existing and emerging risks 
and opportunities, which could affect our 
ability  to  create  value  for  KIP  REIT  and  
stakeholders.
Forward-Looking Statement
This  IAR  2025  includes  forward-looking  
statements   regarding   KIP   REIT’s   plans,   
objectives,     goals,     strategies,     future     
operations    and    performance.    These    
statements      reflect      the      Manager’s      
current  views,  expectations,  beliefs,  and  
assumptions   about   future   events   and   
should  not  be  regarded  as  guarantees  
of    future    performance.    The    actual    
outcomes may differ due to various risks, 
uncertainties   and   factors   beyond   KIP   
REIT’s control. 
Board Statement of Responsibility
The Board acknowledges its responsibility 
to ensure the integrity and accuracy of this 
IAR 2025. In the Board’s opinion, IAR 2025 
addresses  all  key  issues  that  are  material  
to KIP REIT in creating value. IAR 2025 has 
been  prepared  in  accordance  with  the  
IIRC's   Integrated   Reporting   Framework   
and  was  approved  by  the  Board  on  10  
September 2025.

005
INTEGRATED ANNUAL REPORT 2025   |   KIP REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUST
OVERVIEW
KIP   REIT   is   a   Malaysia   domiciled   REIT   
established  on  2  November  2016  pursuant  
to  the  deed  of  trust  dated  2  November  
2016, an amended and restated deed dated 
12  December  2019,  and  a  supplementary  
deed dated 29 September 2020 (collectively 
referred  to  as  the  “Deeds”)  between  the  
Manager  and  Pacific  Trustees  Berhad  (“the  
Trustee”). 
KIP  REIT  was  listed  on  the  Main  Market  of  
Bursa Securities on 6 February 2017. As such, 
our conducts are regulated by the Securities 
Commission  Act  1993,  the  Guidelines  on  
Listed  Real  Estate  Investment  Trusts  (“REIT  
Guidelines”) prescribed by the SC, the MMLR, 
the   Rules   of   Bursa   Malaysia   Depository   
(“Depository”) and taxation laws and rulings. 
Subsequent to our unitholders’ approval on 
29  September  2020,  KIP  REIT’s  investment  
policy  is  to  invest,  directly  and  indirectly,  
in  a  portfolio  of  income  producing  real  
estate  used  primarily  for  retail  purposes,  
and  for  industrial  or  commercial  purposes,  
including,   without   limiting   the   generality   
of   the   foregoing,   warehousing   facilities,   
logistics  facilities  and  manufacturing  sites  
as  well  as  real  estate-related  assets.  As  at  
30 June 2025, KIP REIT’s property portfolio 
consists   of   ten   (10)   community-centric   
malls strategically located in suburban areas 
across   Peninsular   Malaysia   and   four   (4)   
industrial  properties  located  at  Pulau  Indah  
and Cheras Jaya, Selangor.
At   the   heart   of   our   investment   fund   is   our   
community,    with    people    being    central    to    
everything  we  do.  We  foster  a  culture  of  respect,  
collaboration,   and   empowerment,   recognising   
that our success is built on the diverse talents and 
contributions of our team. We strive to serve each 
and every one of our stakeholders with dedication 
to maximise value.
VISION
To be a leading Real Estate Investment 
Trust with sustainability and community 
engagement at the forefront of our 
investment strategies.
MISSION
Creating value for our stakeholders to 
ensure sustainable growth for our 
KIP REIT community.
• For  Our  Investors:  We  strive  to  deliver  
sustainable returns for our investors with 
a  steady  stream  of  distribution  income  
generated   by   our   unique   portfolio   of

assets.
• For  Our  Business  Partners:  We  see  and  
treat our tenants as our business partners. 
We  are  building  a  community  of  assets  
as  a  platform  for  our  business  partners  
to expand their enterprises together with 
our  growing  community  of  properties,  
be  it  local  Small  Medium  Enterprises  
(“SMEs”) or established brands.
• For    Our    Shoppers:    We    want    our    
shoppers  to  feel  at  home  at  all  of  our  
community-centric   malls,   where   they   
can  access  their  daily  necessities  and  
create long-lasting memories with other 
members of their communities.
• For   Our   Employees   :   We   treat   all   
our   people   with   the   utmost   respect,   
embracing     diversity     and     fostering     
inclusion. We are committed to providing 
training opportunities that empower our 
employees to reach their full professional 
potential and promote team growth.
• For Our Community: We are committed 
to helping the communities in our areas 
of  operation  by  supporting  causes  to  
promote    environmental    sustainability    
and   to   foster   economic   and   social   
development.

Investment 
Objective
The  key  objective  is  to  provide  unitholders  with  regular  and  stable  distributions,  
sustainable  long-term  unit  price,  distributable  income  and  capital  growth,  while  
maintaining an appropriate capital structure.
Investment 
Strategies
The  Manager  intends  to  increase  the  income  and  consequently,  the  value  of  the  
investment properties by implementing the following strategies, including: -
• active asset management and enhancement;
• acquisition growth; and
• capital and risk management.
Authorised 
Investments
Real  estate  used  primarily  for  retail  purposes,  and  for  industrial  or  commercial  
purposes,  including,  without  limiting  the  generality  of  the  foregoing,  warehousing  
facilities, logistics facilities and manufacturing sites, special purpose vehicles (“SPVs”), 
real-estate  related  assets,  non-real  estate-related  assets,  cash,  deposits,  money  
market  instruments  and  any  other  investments  not  specified  above  but  specified  as  
a permissible investment in the REIT Guidelines or as otherwise permitted by the SC.
Authorised 
Investment Limits
The investments of KIP REIT are subject to the following investment limits imposed by 
the REIT Guidelines: -
• at least 75.0% of KIP REIT’s Total Asset Value (“TAV”) must be invested in real estate 
and/or SPVs at all times; and
• not more than 25.0% of KIP REIT’s TAV may be invested in non-real estate-related 
assets and/or cash, deposits and money market instruments, 
provided  that  investments  in  both  real  estate-related  assets  and  non-real  estate-
related assets are limited as follows: -
• the value of KIP REIT’s investments in securities issued by any single issuer must not 
exceed 5.0% of KIP REIT’s TAV;

• the value of KIP REIT’s investments in securities issued by any group of companies 
must not exceed 10.0% of KIP REIT’s TAV; and
•  KIP  REIT’s  investments  in  any  class  of  securities  must  not  exceed  10.0%  of  the  
securities issued by any single issuer; or such other limits and investments as may 
be permitted by the SC or the REIT Guidelines.
Borrowing LimitsUp to 50% of the TAV of KIP REIT at the time the borrowings are incurred.
Investors’ ProfileSuitable for investors with long-term investment objectives who seeks regular income 
distribution and long-term capital appreciation, and who understands the risks related 
to the real estate industry and REITs.
Distribution PolicyAt least 90% of KIP REIT’s distributable income shall be distributed on a quarterly basis.

ABOUT THE MANAGER
By virtue of the Deeds, KIP REIT Management Sdn Bhd was appointed to act as the management company of KIP REIT 
on behalf of its unitholders. The Manager is responsible for the administration and management of KIP REIT as well as 
the implementation of KIP REIT’s investment and business strategies.
The Manager is a wholly-owned subsidiary of KIP Homes Sdn Bhd and was incorporated in Malaysia on 15 December 
2015.  The  Manager  also  holds  a  Capital  Markets  and  Services  License  (“CMSL”)  for  the  regulated  activity  of  fund  
management in relation to asset management restricted to REITs.
The Board of the Manager comprises experienced individuals from diverse fields such as finance, compliance, legal, 
human resources, and etc. The corporate structure of the Manager by function is as follows: -

DEAR VALUED STAKEHOLDERS,
It is my pleasure to present our maiden Integrated Annual Report for the financial year ended 30 
June 2025 (“FYE 2025”). 
The global economy continued to grow in 2025, despite the ongoing geopolitical uncertainties. 
Malaysia’s  economy  demonstrated  resilience  in  the  face  of  these  global  challenges.  Gross  
Domestic Product (“GDP”) recorded solid growth of 4.4% in the first quarter of 2025, driven by 
strong domestic demand, a vibrant recovery in the services, manufacturing and tourism sectors 
as  well  as  continued  strength  in  private  consumption.  Meanwhile,  inflation  remained  under  
control, averaging 1.5% in the first quarter of 2025, slightly lower than the 1.8% recorded in the 
previous  year.  Labour  market  conditions  also  improved  meaningfully,  with  the  unemployment  
rate declining to 3.0% in May 2025 from 3.3% in June 2024, reflecting stronger hiring activity and 
growing business confidence in Malaysia. The Overnight Policy Rate (“OPR”) was lowered from 
3.00% to 2.75% in July 2025, marking the first downward adjustment after five (5) years since July 
2020, reflecting a supportive monetary stance conducive to investment and consumption.
Our  financial  results  for  FYE  2025  reflect  both  the  challenges  of  the  external  environment  and  
the strength of KIP REIT’s strategy. KIP REIT has concentrated on delivering consistently for our 
stakeholders and this is reflected in our financial results, capital position and increased income 
distribution  for  unitholders.  KIP  REIT  delivered  a  net  profit  after  tax  ("PAT")  of  RM115.14  million

in  2025,  representing  a  143.3%  increase  from  financial  year  ended  30  June  2024  ("FYE  2024").  
Our capital position and balance sheet remain strong. Reflecting our confidence in the outlook, 
the Board has declared a DPU of 6.80 sen, compared to 6.67 sen in FYE 2024. This reflects our 
ongoing commitment to delivering value to unitholders while maintaining a strong capital position 
to support future growth.

DEAR VALUED STAKEHOLDERS,
I am pleased with KIP REIT’s performance in FYE 2025, which reflects our commitment to driving 
greater sustainable growth and fostering positive impact to our stakeholders. We made meaningful 
progress against our strategic priorities and it has been particularly exciting to see the business 
transition  from  a  focus  on  historic  challenges,  to  concentrating  on  the  opportunities  ahead.  
Our  ability  to  deliver  for  our  stakeholders  remains  at  the  heart  of  everything  we  do,  and  I  am  
enormously proud of our people across the country who have supported our tenants, shoppers 
and partners.
INVESTMENT AND ASSET PERFORMANCE OF KIP REIT
KIP  REIT  recorded  a  higher  revenue  of  RM136.13  million  for  FYE  2025,  
representing  an  increase  of  RM33.97  million  or  33.3%  compared  to  the  FYE  
2024. This growth was primarily driven by higher revenue contribution from 
seven  (7)  KIPMalls,  as  well  as  rental  income  from  the  newly  acquired  retail  
properties, namely TF Value-Mart in Gerik, Perak and DPulze Shopping Centre 
in Cyberjaya and an industrial property in Cheras Jaya, Selangor. 
Furthermore, we are pleased to highlight that our average portfolio occupancy 
rate has improved from 94.1% as at 30 June 2024 to 96.7% as at 30 June 2025. 
This  improvement  was  mainly  attributable  to  recovery  of  KIPMall  Senawang  
upon  introduction  of  new  tenant  namely  ST  Rosyam  and  better  occupancy  
rate across all KIPMalls.

In line with the revenue growth, we recorded a 24.4% increase in NPI for FYE 
2025 as compared to FYE 2024. This improvement supported a 2.0% increase 
in  our  DPU,  reaching  6.80  sen  in  FYE  2025  as  compared  to  6.67  sen  in  FYE  
2024. 
From  an  asset  performance  perspective,  all  properties  within  KIP  REIT  
delivered  solid  and  stable  results.  The  total  market  valuation  of  KIP  REIT’s  
property  portfolio  increased  significantly  to  RM1.49  billion,  up  from  RM1.06  
billion  in  the  previous  financial  year.  This  increase  was  largely  driven  by  the  
inclusion of new properties such as DPulze Shopping Centre, TF Value-Mart, 
and industrial property Lot 35 at Cheras Jaya, as well as better valuation across 
all our properties further affirming the quality and resilience of our portfolio.
During the financial year, we continued to adopt our “2+2” rent model strategy, 
allowing rental revisions every two (2) years instead of being locked into five 
(5)  or  six  (6)  years  term.  This  approach  not  only  provides  flexibility  to  our  
tenants  but  also  enables  us  to  adjust  rental  rates  more  dynamically,  thereby  
ensuring a resilient tenant mix that can adapt to evolving consumer behaviour. 
We also continued to cultivate strong relationships with nearly 1,200 tenants, 
supported by a solid tenant base comprising mainly retailers offering essential 
goods and services. 
As at 30 June 2025, our total assets and total liabilities stood at RM1.58 billion 
and RM0.68 billion respectively, resulting in total unitholders’ funds of RM0.89 
billion.  Our  total  borrowings  were  recorded  at  RM622.78  million,  translating  
to  a  prudent  gearing  ratio  of  39.5%  as  at  30  June  2025.  Overall,  our  NAV  
amounted to RM939.63 million or RM1.18 per unit before income distribution.

YIELD-ACCRETIVE ACQUISITIONS
During FYE 2025, KIP REIT completed three (3) acquisitions, comprising two (2) 
retail  properties  namely  DPulze  Shopping  Centre  in  Cyberjaya  and  TF  Value-
Mart in Gerik, Perak as well as an industrial property in Cheras Jaya, Selangor, 
amounting  to  a  total  cash  consideration  of  RM357.40  million.  All  acquisitions  
were  strategically  selected  based  on  their  favourable  yield  profiles,  secured  
tenancy arrangements and long-term income-generating potential.
These  newly  acquired  assets  have  broadened  the  geographic  diversification  
of  our  portfolio  while  enhancing  the  income  stability  of  the  REIT.  With  these  
additions,   our   portfolio   now   comprises   14   properties,   including   four   (4)   
industrials properties and ten (10) retail malls, with a total NLA exceeding 2.55 
million  square  feet.  We  are  also  proud  to  highlight  that  our  portfolio  average  
occupancy  rate  stood  at  96.7%  for  FYE  2025,  reflecting  the  resilience  and  
stability of our enlarged asset base.  
As part of our strategic expansion, the Trustee entered into three (3) conditional 
Sale and Purchase Agreements (“SPAs”) on 29 August 2024 to acquire three (3) 
industrial properties located across Bintulu, Port Klang and Johor, with a total 
purchase consideration of RM75.70 million. These acquisitions are expected to 
strengthen our industrial asset base and support portfolio diversification.
Subsequently, on 9 April 2025, the Trustee entered into another four (4) conditional 
SPAs for the acquisition of following retail assets, totalling RM118.00 million: -
• KIPMall Desa Coalfields located in Ijok, Selangor;
• Lotus’s Indera Mahkota located in Kuantan, Pahang;
• Three (3) double-storey shop offices with a lower ground car park located

in Kuantan, Pahang; and
• A double-storey commercial building located in Kuantan, Pahang.
These  acquisitions  are  aligned  with  our  strategy  to  enhance  income  stability  
while expanding into underserved regions such as the East Coast and Northern 
regions of Peninsular Malaysia. 
Looking ahead, we are confident that KIP REIT will maintain its growth trajectory, 
leveraging  Malaysia’s  revitalised  industrial  appeal  and  strategic  role  in  global  
supply chain realignment. We remain committed to evaluating yield-accretive 
investment  opportunities  that  support  long-term  growth,  portfolio  resilience  
and consistent value creation for our unitholders.
AEI
Efficient asset management is essential to maintaining the competitiveness and 
appeal of our retail properties. Our AEIs focus on optimising returns, preserving 
asset quality and meeting evolving stakeholder expectations.
In  FYE  2025,  we  completed  several  AEI  projects  across  our  portfolio.  A  key  
milestone  was  the  rollout  of  a  comprehensive  footfall  management  system  
across all retail malls (excluding the newly acquired DPulze Shopping Centre), 
enabling data-driven leasing and marketing decisions.
Other notable enhancements included upgrades to sanitary facilities and prayer 
rooms  at  selected  malls,  a  major  facelift  at  KIPMall  Tampoi,  escalator  and  
landscaping  improvements  at  KIPMall  Bangi,  as  well  as  extensive  rejuvenation  
works at KIPMall Senawang which involved new retail and F&B outlets, upgraded 
air-conditioning and firefighting systems, refreshed entrances, and a dedicated 
51,000 sq ft area to house its new anchor tenant, ST Rosyam. 
Looking ahead, we remain committed to continuous enhancement of our assets 
to strengthen long-term value for our unitholders, tenants and communities.

SUSTAINABLE INITIATIVES
At KIP REIT, we emphasise integrating the EESG practices into our operations. 
Guided by a dedicated Sustainability Working Committee, we have continued 
to   align   our   sustainability   journey   with   16   United   Nations   Sustainable   
Development   Goals   (“UNSDGs”).   These   initiatives   reflect   our   long-term   
dedication to reducing our carbon footprint, optimising energy efficiency and 
enhancing community well-being. 
To  support  green  mobility,  electric  vehicle  ("EV")  charging  stations  have  
been  installed  at  all  KIPMalls  except  Senawang.  Additionally,  measures  were  
introduced  to  improve  toilet  hygiene,  optimise  water  usage,  and  enhance  
operation efficiency through better monitoring and management practices.
KIP  REIT  is  also  accelerating  its  digital  transformation  journey  through  a  
series  of  integrated  initiatives  aimed  at  enhancing  operational  efficiency,  
sustainability  and  stakeholder  value.  These  include  the  implementation  of  
ServeDeck Apps to streamline mall operations with centralised management, 
real-time  monitoring  and  automated  processes,  as  well  as  the  expansion  of  
solar photovoltaic systems to reduce energy costs and environmental impact. 
KIP  REIT  is  also  advancing  its  sustainability-linked  financing  framework  to  
align capital strategies with EESG commitments, deepening its collaboration 
with KJTS Group Berhad to drive energy efficiency across its properties, and 
continuing  to  support  community-focused  programmes  that  foster  social  
engagement and inclusivity.
Looking  ahead,  we  remain  focused  on  advancing  our  climate  resilience  
strategy through practical and responsible actions. Wherever feasible, we will 
implement energy efficiency upgrades across our properties, invest in verified 
carbon  offset  projects,  and  strengthen  our  risk  management  by  embedding  
climate-related  considerations  into  our  Enterprise  Risk  Management  ("ERM")  
Framework.  We  also  look  forward  to  adopting  IFRS  S2  disclosures  and  are  
committed  to  enhancing  our  data  governance  infrastructure  to  ensure  that  
our  sustainability  reporting  is  transparent,  robust  and  aligned  with  global  
standards.
As  our  operations  increasingly  leverage  digital  solutions  to  support  these  
initiatives,   safeguarding   information   technology   ("IT")   systems   and   data   
has  become  equally  critical.  In  compliance  with  the  latest  SC’s  Guidelines  
on  Technology  Risk  Management,  we  have  formalised  and  put  in  place  a  
Technology  Risk  Management  Framework  to  guide  KIP  REIT’s  management  
of technology risks, technology operations, technology service providers and 
cybersecurity. We also continued to engage our outsourced IT service provider 
to strengthen the resilience of our IT infrastructure against cybersecurity risks 
and continued to provide cybersecurity awareness training for our employees.

Malaysia’s economy is set to stay on solid footing in 2025, with Bank Negara Malaysia ("BNM") projecting GDP growth

The principal investment policy of KIP REIT is to invest directly and/or indirectly in a diversified portfolio of income-

long-term capital growth for unitholders. Nevertheless, in consultation with the Trustee and subject to all applicable 
laws, regulations and requirements, the Manager may, from time to time, adjust KIP REIT’s investment policy to align 
with evolving market opportunities and the Trust’s strategic objectives.

changes to the stated investment policy must be approved by unitholders through a resolution passed by not less than 
two-thirds (2/3) of all unitholders present and voting at a duly convened meeting in accordance with the provisions of 
the Deeds.

Gross revenue from our retail segment increased by RM34.07 million or 35.8% from RM95.06 million in FYE 2024 to 
RM129.13 million in the current financial year. This increase was primarily driven by rental income recognised from the 
newly acquired properties as well as higher rental income derived from all of our KIPMalls as the overall occupancy 
rates in our KIPMalls increased from 89.2% in FYE 2024 to 93.9% in in FYE 2025.
Gross revenue from the central region increased significantly by RM35.81 million or 179.5% from RM19.95 million in FYE 
2024 to RM55.76 million in FYE 2025. The increase was mainly driven by the recognition of rental income amounting to 
RM22.98 million from our newly acquired shopping mall, DPulze Shopping Centre. In addition, rental income from several 
KIPMalls in particular, KIPMall Kota Warisan, KIPMall Bangi and KIPMall Senawang also recorded notable improvements 
due to higher occupancy rates during the financial year, which stood at 99.2%, 87.4% and 85.1% respectively.
Meanwhile,  gross  revenue  from  the  southern  region  increased  by  RM1.93  million  or  3.7%  from  RM52.08  million  in  
FYE 2024 to RM54.01 million in FYE 2025. This growth was mainly driven by the recognition of higher rental income 
from  KIPMall  Melaka,  KIPMall  Tampoi  and  KIPMall  Masai,  due  to  higher  occupancy  rate  of  98.1%,  97.7%  and  97.2%  
respectively, as well as higher rental per square feet upon renewal.
Industrial Segment
Gross revenue derived from our industrial segment declined marginally by RM0.09 million or 1.3% from RM7.10 million in 
FYE 2024 to RM7.01 million in the current financial year mainly due to the MFRS 16 accounting adjustment recognised. 
Nevertheless, the impact was partially offset by the recognition of rental income amounting to RM0.60 million from our 
newly acquired industrial property, Sin Chee Heng (Lot 35).
NPI
KIP REIT recorded higher NPI of RM96.82 million in FYE 2025 as compared to RM77.82 million in FYE 2024, with retail 
segment contributing the majority at 92.8% of the total NPI. Overall, the portfolio achieved an NPI margin of 71.1%, with 
the retail and industrial segments having NPI margin of 69.6% and 99.4% respectively.
Compared  to  properties  in  the  retail  segment,  industrial  properties  are  able  to  yield  a  higher  NPI  as  most  property  
operating expenses such as utilities, maintenance, upkeep and repairs expenses are borne by the tenants.

OPERATION REVIEW
Tenant Management
KIP  REIT  continues  to  implement  a  dynamic  leasing  strategy  focused  on  stable  and  sustainable  income  from  its  
community-centric  mall  portfolio.  As  at  30  June  2025,  total  tenancies  across  all  seven  (7)  KIPMalls  and  the  DPulze  
Shopping  Centre  stood  at  1,172  tenancies,  representing  a  significant  increase  of  25.1%  from  937  tenancies  in  the  
previous financial year. Collectively, these tenants occupied approximately 1,495,338 square feet, equivalent to 97.1% 
of the total NLA of 1,539,273 square feet.
In addition, KIP REIT has a long-term master lease agreement with Aeon Mall Kinta City until 2030, as well as a long-
term  triple  net  master  lease  agreement  with  TF  Value-Mart  up  to  2039.  These  agreements  provide  strong  income  
visibility as we are able to maintain a 100.0% occupancy rate throughout the respective lease periods. 
During FYE 2025, KIP REIT maintained 100.0% occupancy rate in a few assets including, Aeon Mall Kinta City, TF Value-
Mart and all four (4) industrial factories. KIP REIT’s overall occupancy rate has also improved to 96.7% as compared to

94.1% in the previous financial year. 
Retail Tenancy Expiry Profile
KIP REIT is strategically positioned with tenancy durations tailored to the business nature of each tenant, offering longer 
lease  tenures  to  key  and  anchor  tenants.  This  diversification  across  the  portfolio  efficiently  mitigates  risk  related  to  
tenant concentration. 
As at 30 June 2025, the weighted average lease expiry (“WALE”) stood at 3.0 years by ONLA, compared to 1.9 years in 
FYE 2024. By GRI, the WALE was 2.3 years, reflecting an upward trend from 1.6 years in FYE 2024. These increases were 
mainly attributed to the renewal of major tenancy agreements in a few KIPMalls which expired during the financial year. 
The longer WALE aligns with KIP REIT’s management strategies and business model which aims to strengthen portfolio 
stability  while  optimising  rental  income  through  adjustments  to  rental  rates  at  lease  renewals,  ensuring  that  lease  
agreements remain competitive and reflective of prevailing market conditions and tenant requirements.

MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS
RETAIL MARKET OVERVIEW
The Malaysia’s retail sector is undergoing a structural transformation, driven by the rapid expansion of e-commerce, 
ongoing digital innovation and evolving consumer lifestyle preferences. Traditional shopping malls are shifting beyond 
their  conventional  transactional  role  to  become  lifestyle  and  community  hubs,  integrating  retail  with  dining,  leisure,  
wellness and social interaction. This evolution is creating a more engaging, experience-driven environment that attracts 
and retains a broader spectrum of consumers.
E-commerce  growth  continues  to  accelerate,  underpinned  by  high  internet  and  mobile  penetration,  greater  digital  
adoption and shifting purchasing behaviours. The rise of social commerce, omnichannel retail strategies and seamless 
integration  between  online  and  offline  platforms  is  redefining  the  retail  landscape.  In  this  changing  environment,  
suburban retail malls that cater to essential daily needs and foster community engagement remain resilient, providing 
convenience and social interaction that online platforms cannot fully replicate.
Despite pressures from rising operational costs and cautious consumer sentiment amid global economic uncertainties, 
domestic retail spending has improved, shifting from prestige to masstige, a transition that corresponds well with the 
positioning of our retail malls and enhances our competitive advantage. This resilience is supported by government 
measures such as targeted financial assistance, adjustments to the national minimum wage, inflation control policies 
and  promotional  initiatives.  The  upcoming  Visit  Malaysia  2026  campaign  is  also  expected  to  boost  tourism-related  
retail activity, generating positive spillover effects for the sector.
Looking  ahead,  the  integration  of  technology,  data-driven  personalisation  and  customer-centric  strategies  will  be  
essential in maintaining competitiveness, while the incorporation of diverse lifestyle amenities will remain a key driver 
of long-term growth in the Malaysia’s retail sector.
INDUSTRIAL MARKET OVERVIEW
Momentum  in  Malaysia’s  industrial  sector  remained  robust  in  2025,  driven  by  sustained  manufacturing  activity  and  
the  continued  expansion  of  e-commerce,  which  together  underpinned  strong  demand  for  modern  logistics  and  
warehousing facilities. The rapid growth in online retail has intensified the need for efficient distribution and fulfilment 
centres, encouraging businesses to seek strategically located, technology-enabled industrial spaces that support fast 
and reliable supply chains.
National  strategic  initiatives  such  as  the  Johor–Singapore  Special  Economic  Zone  and  targeted  tax  incentives  for  
flagship  developments,  including  the  Smart  Logistics  Complex,  further  reinforce  Malaysia’s  standing  as  a  preferred  
destination for regional supply chain investments. 
Furthermore, the ongoing infrastructure enhancements and improved connectivity across key industrial hubs such as 
Klang Valley, Johor and Penang, have also played a pivotal role in attracting both domestic and foreign investors. These 
developments  have  supported  steady  inflow  of  foreign  direct  investment  into  strategic  infrastructure  projects  such  
as the East Coast Rail Link and the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone. The logistics sector, including last-mile 
delivery facilities and smart warehouses, has also experienced especially strong demand as supply chain models evolve 
in response to global trade dynamics.

Key Trend 1: Macroeconomy
What Happened in FYE 2025
Malaysia’s GDP expanded by 4.4% in the first quarter of 2025, driven by strong domestic demand. Such expansion was 
mainly attributed to resilient household spending and a steady expansion in investment activities, both underpinned by 
supportive labour market conditions, income-related policy and the progress of multi-year projects in both the public 
and private sectors. In the external sector, export growth was slower mainly due to lower mining exports. However, 
this was partially offset by stronger electrical and electronics (“E&E”) exports and tourism activity. On the supply side, 
growth was driven by the services and manufacturing sectors, supported by higher Government services and strong 
E&E production respectively. 
As a result, BNM maintained the OPR at 3.0% throughout FYE 2025, a level held since May 2023. Headline and core 
inflation  averaged  1.5%  and  1.9%  respectively  in  the  first  quarter  of  2025,  reflecting  moderate  global  costs  and  the  
absence of excessive domestic demand pressures.
On 18 October 2024, the Malaysian Government announced the Budget 2025 which is Malaysia’s largest ever budget 
at  RM421.00  billion,  comprising  RM335.00  billion  for  operating  expenditure  and  RM86.00  billion  for  development.  
This is the third budget formulated based on the Ekonomi MADANI framework, focusing on revitalising the economy, 
catalysing  transformative  change  and  improving  the  overall  well-being  of  the  local  community.  In  particular,  the  
Malaysian  Government  rolled  out  targeted  subsidies,  such  as  fuel  subsidies,  to  cushion  households  and  businesses  
against rising living costs. The allocation for Sumbangan Tunai Ramah (“STR”), Sumbangan Asas Ramah (“SARA”) and 
Department of Social Welfare was also increased to provide greater support for the local community. A further RM1.00 
billion was channelled to broaden efforts in addressing the cost of living, including the expansion of Payung RAHMAH 
initiative and collaborations with supermarket operators, wholesale markets, retail stores, farmers' markets, cooperatives 
to stabilise prices of essential goods. To further safeguard livelihoods, the Malaysian Government has announced an 
increase in the minimum wage from RM1,500 to RM1,700 per month, effective 1 February 2025.
Labour  market  conditions  also  strengthened,  with  the  unemployment  rate  stood  at  3.0%  in  June  2025,  marking  the  
lowest  level  since  the  pandemic  and  signalling  continued  strength  in  job  creation  and  income  stability.  Meanwhile,  
headline Consumer Price Index (“CPI”) in June 2025 was recorded at +1.1% year-over-year (“YoY’), marking the lowest 
level  since  the  pandemic,  while  the  core  CPI  recorded  at  +1.8%  YoY  in  June  2025,  indicating  subdued  underlying  
inflationary pressures. 
Externally,  FYE  2025  was  marked  by  heightened  global  market  volatility.  On  2  April  2025,  the  United  States  (“US”)  
Government announced a reciprocal tariff of 24.0% on Malaysia, contributing to increased uncertainties in the global 
trade environment amid other ongoing trade negotiations and geopolitical tensions. Despite prevailing downside risks 
in the global economic environment, BNM has reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining a monetary policy stance that 
supports sustainable economic growth while ensuring price stability.

Malaysia. At the same time, evolving sustainability trend and accelerating technology 
adoption created both challenges and opportunities that we were able to capitalise on 
to strengthen our long-term business sustainability.

Amid prevailing global uncertainties, BNM has revised its projected GDP growth for 2025 to a range of 4.0% to 4.8% on

services, education services as well as wellness or beauty services. However, certain essential goods remain exempted 
from sales tax, while Malaysian citizens are exempted from service tax on healthcare and education services.

of customer activity types (i.e., residential, commercial or industrial), together with the implementation of Automatic 
Fuel Adjustment (“AFA”) and Time of Use (“TOU”) scheme, is expected to deliver cost savings for us as most of our malls 
operate  on  lower  voltage  levels.  For  our  high-voltage  consumption  malls,  we  will  continue  to  closely  monitor  and  
manage our electricity usage effectively.

Key Trend 2: Evolving Consumer Behaviour
What Happened in FYE 2025
Retail Group Malaysia Sdn Bhd (“RGM”) reported a 5.6% growth in retail sales in the first quarter of 2025, driven by festive 
spending during Chinese New Year and Hari Raya Aidilfitri, month-long national school holidays as well as increased 
tourist arrivals due to favourable exchange rate and visa-free entry for visitors from China and India. Specifically, the 
combined department store and supermarket subsector recorded positive growth of 5.8%, where the department store 
subsector expanded by 2.7% and the supermarket and hypermarket subsector posted encouraging growth of 3.7%. The 
F&B establishments also experienced a surge in sales, with cafés and restaurants grew by 6.5%, while take-away outlets, 
kiosks and stalls recorded a stronger growth of 12.3%.
Despite Malaysia’s economic growth, United Overseas Bank’s ASEAN Consumer Sentiment Study 2024 highlighted a 
decline in public confidence due to negative emotions, recession fears, rising household expenses and concerns over 
financial  stability.  Consumers  are  now  prioritising  essentials  such  as  groceries,  education  and  utilities,  while  cutting  
back on insurance, investment and non-essential spending.
At  the  same  time,  Malaysian  consumers  increasingly  seek  convenient  and  immersive  shopping  experiences,  driven  
by  continuous  technological  innovations  that  are  reshaping  the  retail  landscape.  Traditionally,  online  and  offline  
transactions  are  treated  separately  and  not  integrated,  leading  to  a  fragmented  and  poor  shopping  experience.

physical  shopping  experiences,  especially  among  Gen-Z  consumers.  Innovations  such  as  self-checkout  kiosks  and

Key Trend 3: Sustainability and Environmental Concerns
What Happened in FYE 2025
2024 marked a concerning turning point in the global climate trajectory, with the World Meteorological Organisation 
(“WMO”)  reporting  that  the  global  average  surface  temperature  reached  1.55°C  above  pre-industrial  levels  (with  a  
margin  of  uncertainty  of  ±0.13°C).  This  is  the  first  calendar  year  in  which  the  temperature  has  exceeded  the  1.50°C  
threshold set in the Paris Agreement, underscoring the urgent call for accelerated climate action.
According to the Malaysia Meteorological Department, the average temperature in Peninsular Malaysia has increased 
by 0.24°C per decade since 1969. As warming intensifies, Malaysia faces shifting climate patterns with more frequent 
disasters and extreme weather events such as heat waves, floods, droughts, forest fires and sea level rise. These impacts 
threaten  not  only  local  community  but  also  public  health,  agriculture  and  food  security,  infrastructure,  and  energy  
systems, ultimately placing greater strain on the economy and environment. To this end, Malaysia’s Ministry of Natural 
Resources and Environmental Sustainability launched the National Climate Change Policy 2.0 on 30 September 2024, 
reinforcing Malaysia’s commitment and strategies to addressing this pressing environmental challenge.

Key Trend 4: Technology and Digital Transformation
What Happened in FYE 2025
According  to  CyberSecurity  Malaysia,  a  total  of  6,888  cyber  incidents  were  recorded  in  Malaysia  during  FYE  2025,  
primarily involving fraud, content-related issue, intrusion and malicious code. This marked a 12.4% increase from 6,128 
cyber incidents reported in FYE 2024, highlighting the escalating risks faced by businesses and individuals. This reinforces 
the importance of strengthening cybersecurity measures to protect against increasingly sophisticated threats. 
While digital transformation continues to bring tremendous benefits to Malaysia’s economy, cybersecurity threats have 
grown  more  severe.  To  maintain  strong  cyber  hygiene,  digitalisation  must  be  accompanied  by  robust  and  resilient  
cybersecurity measures.
In response, the SC revised its Guidelines on Technology Risk Management, effective from 19 August 2024, requiring 
capital market participants to report near miss incidents, conduct cybersecurity assessments and perform penetration 
testing before deploying critical systems. Meanwhile, the Malaysian Government also enforced the Cyber Security Act 
2024, effective from 26 August 2024, covering key cybersecurity features such as the establishment of National Cyber 
Security Committee, clear functions and duties of the National Critical Information Infrastructure (“NCII”) sector leads, 
management of cyber security threats and incidents related to NCII, and provisions to regulate cyber security service 
providers through licencing.
The  growing  severity  of  cybersecurity  threats  in  
Malaysia  heightens  the  necessity  for  KIP  REIT  to  
embed  robust  and  resilient  measures  within  our  
operations.  Any  lapse  in  management  may  lead  to  
cyber incidents that could potentially cause financial 
losses,   legal   liabilities   and   reputational   damage,   
ultimately affecting stakeholders’ trust on KIP REIT.
To  address  these  risks,  increased  operational  costs  
may   be   incurred   for   investment   in   technology   
infrastructure,     system     upgrades     and     skilled     
cybersecurity  professionals.  These  measures  shall  
reduce the risk of cyber incidents that could disrupt 
operations or compromise sensitive data. 
Meanwhile,  the  implementation  of  the  SC’s  revised  
Guidelines  on  Technology  Risk  Management  and  
the  enforcement  of  the  Cyber  Security  Act  2024  
are  expected  to  strengthen  KIP  REIT’s  cybersecurity  
framework, providing an additional safeguard against 
emerging cyber threats.
KIP REIT remains committed to ensuring compliance 
with applicable rules and regulations by continuously 
strengthening  our  internal  controls.  To  this  end,  
the   Manager   has   formalised   a   Technology   Risk   
Management Framework and carried out an IT disaster 
recovery  exercise,  which  involved  the  upgrading  of  
its existing IT system to enhance resilience.
In addition, we continued to engage our outsourced 
IT service provider to strengthen the resilience of our 
IT  infrastructure.  Cybersecurity  awareness  trainings  
were  also  conducted  for  all  employees,  covering  IT  
security  best  practices,  data  handling  procedures,  
data  protection  measures  and  the  identification  of  
potential cyber threats. 
How It Impacts KIP REITActions/Strategies
FYE 2026 Outlook
Through Budget 2025, the Malaysian Government has taken significant steps to enhance the nation’s cybersecurity in 
response to the rising frequency and severity of cyber threats. Key measures include an allocation of RM20.00 million 
to expand the role of the National Fraud Response Centre, supported by the launch of the National Fraud Portal which 
is  designed  to  facilitate  the  automatic  detection  of  suspicious  transactions  to  combat  online  fraud  more  effectively.  
Besides, legislative enhancements through amendments to the Penal Code (Act 574) and the Criminal Procedure Code 
(Act 593) empower enforcement agencies with greater authority to take more effective action against mule account 
syndicates.
Aligning  with  the  enactment  of  the  Cyber  Security  Act  2024,  the  National  Cyber  Security  Agency  will  be  further  
strengthened through an additional budget allocation of RM10.00 million and the addition of 100 new staff positions. 
Collectively, these measures are expected to reinforce Malaysia’s cyber resilience, safeguard national’s cybersecurity 
environment and enhance public trust and confidence in the digital economy.

holding  all  properties  under  portfolio  of  KIP  REIT  (“KIP

our unitholders.

follows a tiered approach, with the REIT Manager serving 
as  the  management  company  overseeing  investment  
strategy   and   governance,   while   Nawawi   Tie   Leung   
Property  Consultants  Sdn.  Bhd.  is  appointed  by  REIT  
Manager as the property manager of KIP REIT (“Property 
Manager”)  through  a  formalised  agreement  established  
with the concurrence of the REIT Trustee.

distinct asset classes:

operated through the Property Manager, serving as 
vibrant neighbourhood commercial hubs
• Leased-Out  Assets:  Properties  owned  by  KIP  REIT  
and  leased  to  tenants  under  long-term  tenancy  
agreements, generating recurring rental income

management,  our  Property  Manager  has  implemented

allocates resources according to asset type requirements.

Sustainability Reporting Scope
This    SR2025    encompasses    a    focused    reporting    
framework   that   primarily   addresses   Managed   Assets 
and their sustainability performance. It excludes Leased-
Out   Assets   from   standard   reporting   metrics   except   
where  explicitly  specified.  All  sustainability  indicators,  
metrics, targets, and benchmarks apply exclusively to our 
Managed Assets portfolio.
Within  the  Managed  Assets  category,  all  environmental  
performance   data   for   DPulze   Shopping   Centre   has

acquisition   completion   on   12   December   2024.   This   
exclusion  allows  for  proper  integration  and  operational  
stabilisation, with comprehensive data collection for this

Human Capital Reporting Structure

REIT  directly  reimburses  the  Service  Provider  for  all  
employee compensation (including salaries, allowances,

Service Provider’s employees as integral members of the 
KIP REIT workforce.

Governance Structure  
KIP REIT institutionalises sustainability through a structured governance framework designed to ensure accountability, 
transparency,  and  effective  execution  of  sustainability  initiatives.  This  framework  is  designed  to  align  sustainability  
priorities  with  our  overall  business  strategy,  ensuring  that  ethical  conduct,  risk  management,  and  long-term  value  
creation remain at the forefront of our operations.
Our sustainability governance operates through a multi-tiered structure, delineating roles and responsibilities across

different levels of leadership and management.
The  following  governance  structure  illustrates  the  hierarchy  and  interaction  between  these  key  bodies,  providing  a  
transparent overview of how KIP REIT steers its sustainability agenda from strategic oversight to operational execution.
Roles and Responsibilities
SUSTAINABILITY GOVERNANCE
At  the  apex  of  KIP  REIT’s  sustainability  governance  framework,  the  Board  of  Directors  (“BOD”)  holds  
ultimate accountability for setting the strategic tone and overarching direction of KIP REIT’s sustainability 
agenda.  This  responsibility  reflects  our  unwavering  commitment  to  upholding  the  highest  standards  of  
integrity,  transparency,  and  responsible  business  conduct.  The  BOD  ensures  that  governance  practices  
anchored  in  strong  ethical  principles  serve  as  the  foundation  for  embedding  sustainability  goals  and  
objectives into the REIT’s long-term corporate strategy. In fulfilling this role, the BOD rigorously reviews 
and approves key sustainability strategies, comprehensive policies, and material sustainability matters that 
are  critical  to  KIP  REIT’s  sustainable  growth.  It  also  oversees  the  outcomes  of  materiality  assessments,  
which prioritise sustainability issues based on their significance to stakeholders and potential impact on 
the business, thereby guiding focused resource allocation and risk management.
The  BOD  actively  supervises  stakeholder  engagement  processes  to  ensure  meaningful  dialogue  with  
investors, tenants, regulators, and other key parties, enabling KIP REIT to better anticipate and manage 
sustainability  risks  and  opportunities.  Furthermore,  the  BOD  continuously  monitors  the  progress  and  
performance  against  established  sustainability  targets,  ensuring  that  these  objectives  are  met  within  
agreed  timelines.  This  oversight  extends  to  integrating  sustainability  considerations  into  the  REIT’s  
broader  strategic  planning,  balancing  economic  returns  with  environmental  stewardship  and  social  
responsibility. Through these comprehensive responsibilities, the Board fosters a culture of accountability 
and leadership for sustainability that permeates all levels of the organisation, reinforcing KIP REIT’s position 
as a responsible and forward-looking real estate investment trust.
To support the BOD in executing its sustainability mandate effectively, KIP REIT has established dedicated 
governance bodies, including the Sustainability Steering Committee (“SSC”) and the Sustainability Working 
Group (“SWG”). These committee and working group collaborate closely to oversee, guide, and implement 
sustainability initiatives, ensuring that Environmental, Social, and Governance (“ESG”) considerations are 
systematically integrated into decision-making frameworks and operational practices across KIP REIT.
The SSC, chaired by the Chief Sustainability Officer and comprising key senior managers such as the Legal 
and Compliance Manager, the Chief Operating Officer of Southern Region and the Chief Finance Officer, 
is primarily responsible for the strategic oversight of ESG matters. Its scope includes:
 Reviewing and recommending the ESG framework, policies, and sustainability strategies to the 
BOD for approval
 Advising the BOD on emerging sustainability trends, risks, and opportunities, including climate-
related issues
 Ensuring compliance with relevant regulations and sustainability reporting standards.
 Developing ESG goals, targets, and key performance indicators (“KPIs”) aligned with KIP REIT’s 
environmental and stakeholder requirements
 Monitoring and reporting on sustainability performance to the BOD
 Facilitating communication between the BOD and management on sustainability topic
 Leading efforts to embed a culture of sustainability, including initiatives to reduce environmental 
impact and enhance social value
 Overseeing the integration of sustainability into business operations and tracking performance 
against set targets
Essentially,  the  SSC  functions  as  the  strategic  steering  body  that  sets  direction,  ensures  regulatory  
alignment, and monitors overall sustainability performance at a high level.

 Coordinating and driving sustainability initiatives across KIP REIT’s portfolio and business units
  Engaging  with  stakeholders,  including  property  manager,  to  embed  ESG  considerations  into  
operational practices

Monitoring progress of sustainability initiatives and reporting findings to the SSC.

guidelines, GRI Standards, and other frameworks.
The  SWG  acts  as  the  execution  arm,  translating  strategic  ESG  goals  into  concrete  actions,  managing  
risks  and  opportunities  at  the  operational  level,  and  ensuring  continuous  improvement  in  sustainability  
performance.
Together,  the  SSC  and  SWG  collaborate  closely  through  quarterly  meetings,  where  they  review  ESG  
matters,  assess  progress  against  targets,  and  address  emerging  sustainability  issues.  This  structured  
interaction ensures alignment between strategic oversight and operational execution, enabling KIP REIT 
to maintain a dynamic and responsive sustainability governance framework that supports its long-term 
value creation and commitment to responsible business practices.
This  clear  delineation  of  roles  between  the  SSC’s  strategic  governance  and  the  SWG’s  operational  
management  strengthens  KIP  REIT’s  ability  to  integrate  sustainability  into  all  aspects  of  its  business  
effectively.
At the operational level, the SWG is further empowered by the expertise and resources of KIP REIT’s two 
key operational arms: the REIT Manager and the Service Provider. 
Each of these entities is structured with specialised units including Finance, Legal, Compliance, Sustainability, 
Information  Technology,  Human  Resources,  Leasing,  Operations,  and  Mechanical  &  Electrical  (“M&E”) 
that provide targeted technical expertise and drive the execution of sustainability initiatives within their 
respective domains.
By leveraging the capabilities of these specialised units, KIP REIT ensures that sustainability practices are 
embedded  at  the  ground  level.  This  approach  enables  the  effective  management  of  assets,  proactive  
tenant engagement, and the pursuit of operational efficiency, all while upholding KIP REIT’s sustainability 
objectives.

Sustainability-linked KPIs 
KIP REIT underscores its unwavering commitment to sustainability by embedding comprehensive KPIs into the collective 
scorecards  of  its  Executive  Directors,  senior  management,  and  all  operational  divisions.  These  collective  scorecards  
function as a collaborative, team-based performance appraisal system, where employees are evaluated not solely on 
individual accomplishments but also on their collective contributions towards achieving KIP REIT’s sustainability goals. 
This approach fosters a culture of shared responsibility and collective ownership of sustainability outcomes across the 
entire organisation.
The sustainability KPIs incorporated into these scorecards are carefully aligned with KIP REIT’s material ESG priorities, 
reflecting  KIP  REIT’s  strategic  focus  areas.  The  performance  against  these  KPIs  is  directly  tied  to  the  funding  and  
distribution  of  annual  bonus  pools  within  each  Department,  thereby  creating  a  clear  and  tangible  link  between  
sustainability  performance  and  remuneration  for  both  executive  management  and  employees.  This  linkage  ensures  
that sustainability is not an abstract goal but an integral part of KIP REIT’s performance and reward system.
Specifically, the sustainability KPIs for KIP REIT encompass a broad spectrum of critical initiatives. These include the 
systematic  integration  of  sustainability  practices  into  the  day-to-day  management  of  KIP  REIT’s  property  portfolio,  
with  Executive  Directors  tasked  to  identify  relevant  ESG  measures  and  promote  sustainability  initiatives.  To  ensure  
accountability  and  measurable  progress  across  the  organisation,  each  department  has  been  assigned  specific  
sustainability targets that align with our overarching ESG objectives:
Finance Department• Conduct finance-related trainings
Operation Department• Reduce energy consumption
• Reduce water consumption
• Reduce total wasted generated
• Increase waste recycle rate
HR Department• Increase the training hours
Sustainability Department • Develop and implement key sustainability policies, including Climate Risk 
Management, Energy Management, and Waste Management
By  embedding  sustainability  KPIs  within  its  performance  management  and  compensation  frameworks,  KIP  REIT  not  
only reinforces accountability and drives continuous improvement but also signals to stakeholders its commitment to 
sustainable value creation. This integrated approach ensures that sustainability considerations are deeply woven into 
the  fabric  of  KIP  REIT’s  strategy,  operations  and  culture,  ultimately  contributing  to  long-term  resilience,  stakeholder  
trust, and positive environmental and social impact.
Driving Sustainable Growth through Governance and Incentives
KIP REIT’s robust sustainability governance framework, seamlessly integrated with performance-linked remuneration, 
reflects  its  unwavering  dedication  to  embedding  ESG  principles  at  the  heart  of  its  business.  By  clearly  defining

responsibilities from the BOD down to operational teams and fostering close collaboration between strategic oversight 
and  day-to-day  execution,  KIP  REIT  ensures  sustainability  is  a  core  driver  of  all  decision-making  and  operational  
activities.
Embedding sustainability KPIs into collective scorecards and compensation mechanisms not only drives accountability 
but also empowers every member of the organisation to actively contribute toward achieving KIP REIT’s sustainability 
ambitions.  This  comprehensive  and  cohesive  approach  enhances  operational  resilience,  builds  lasting  stakeholder  
confidence,  and  positions  KIP  REIT  as  a  leader  in  responsible  real  estate  investment.  Ultimately,  it  demonstrates  KIP  
REIT’s commitment to creating sustainable, long-term value for investors, tenants, communities, and the environment,

SUSTAINABILITY FRAMEWORK AND POLICIES
KIP  REIT’s  Sustainability  Framework  is  the  foundation  for  embedding  responsible  and  forward-looking  sustainability  
practices  across  our  operations  and  investment  strategies.  This  framework  is  both  comprehensive  and  adaptive,  
ensuring that sustainability is not a standalone initiative but an integral part of our value creation and risk management

processes.
KIP REIT’s Strategic Visions: Pillars of Sustainable Growth
At the heart of our framework are four interdependent pillars, each representing a strategic vision that guides all our 
sustainability  initiatives  and  policies.  These  visions  define  our  commitment  to  fostering  a  sustainable  future  while  
delivering consistent returns for our unitholders.
ECONOMIC PILLAR
VISION 1 
Powering Sustainable Economic Growth 
Economic  performance  and  resilience  at  KIP  REIT  are  intrinsically  linked  to  the  long-term  sustainability  of  our  
assets, tenants and the communities we serve. Recognising that real estate investment extends beyond financial 
returns, we proactively address operational and market risks while supporting sustainable economic development 
within our portfolio and value chain.
We collaborate with tenants, property managers and local partners to identify operational efficiencies, promote 
responsible  business  practices,  and  encourage  innovation  that  drives  shared  value.  By  integrating  sustainability  
considerations  into  our  investment  decisions  and  asset  management,  we  aim  to  future-proof  our  properties,  
enhance income stability for our unitholders, and contribute to the economic vitality of the communities in which 
we operate.
Our  commitment  to  sustainable  economic  growth  is  reflected  in  prudent  financial  management,  transparent  
reporting, and the pursuit of strategic investments that generate long-term benefits for all stakeholders. Through 
these efforts, KIP REIT seeks to set a benchmark for resilience and sustainable value creation in the Malaysian REIT 
sector.
GOVERNANCE PILLAR
VISION 2 
Championing Integrity and Transparency 
At KIP REIT, robust governance is fundamental to building trust, managing risk, and ensuring long-term organisational 
resilience. We recognise that effective governance extends beyond compliance, shaping our culture and influencing 
every decision we make. Our commitment is reflected in the continuous strengthening of our internal controls, risk 
management processes, and ethical standards.
We  actively  engage  our  Board  of  Director,  Senior  Management,  and  employees  in  upholding  integrity  and  
transparency  through  clear  policies  on  anti-bribery  and  corruption,  whistleblowing,  conflicts  of  interest,  cyber  
security and data privacy. By fostering a culture of integrity, accountability and transparency, we can anticipate and 
address emerging risks, safeguard stakeholder interests, and maintain regulatory compliance.
Through  transparent  communication,  rigorous  oversight,  and  ongoing  capacity  building,  KIP  REIT  aims  to  set  a  
benchmark for ethical conduct and governance excellence within the Malaysian REIT industry.

ENVIRONMENTAL PILLAR
VISION 3
Pioneering the Net Zero Transition
KIP REIT is committed to leading the transition toward a low-carbon, resource-efficient future. We recognise the 
significant role the real estate sector plays in addressing climate change and environmental challenges. Our strategy 
is focused on integrating environmental stewardship into every facet of our operations and investment lifecycle.
We work closely with tenants, service providers and industry partners to implement energy-efficient technologies, 
reduce  greenhouse  gas  emissions,  and  advance  sustainable  waste  and  resource  management  practices.  Regular  
assessments of climate-related risks and opportunities inform our approach, ensuring our portfolio’s resilience and 
alignment with national and global sustainability goals.
By prioritising innovation, continuous improvement, and transparent environmental reporting, KIP REIT strives to be at 
the forefront of environmental leadership, supporting the net zero transition and delivering value for all stakeholders.
SOCIAL PILLAR
VISION 4
Enriching Human Capital and Social Ecosystem
We  believe  that  the  strength  and  sustainability  of  KIP  REIT  are  rooted  in  the  well-being  of  our  people  and  the  
communities we serve. Our social strategy is designed to foster a diverse, inclusive and supportive environment for 
employees, tenants and local stakeholders.
We actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion, uphold human rights and labour standards, and invest in health, 
safety, and wellness initiatives. Through regular engagement and collaborative partnerships, we seek to understand 
stakeholder needs and deliver targeted community development programmes that create lasting positive impact.
By  nurturing  talent,  supporting  social  resilience,  and  championing  community  investment,  KIP  REIT  aims  to  
contribute meaningfully to the broader social ecosystem, ensuring that our growth is shared and sustainable.

MATERIALITY
ASSESSMENT
In  the  evolving  landscape  of  the  REIT  sector,  there  is  an  increasing  focus  on  transparency  and  accountability  in  
sustainability  practices,  driven  by  heightened  stakeholder  expectations  and  regulatory  demands.  At  KIP  REIT,  we  
recognise  the  critical  importance  of  integrating  sustainability  into  our  core  operations  and  strategic  initiatives.  Our  
approach  to  identifying  and  prioritising  key  sustainability  matters  is  fundamental  to  enhancing  our  Environmental,  
Social, and Governance (“ESG”) performance and driving long-term value creation.
Our  material  matters  represent  the  issues  that  are  most  critical  to  our  business  and  stakeholders,  guiding  us  in  the  
development  of  strategies  and  initiatives  that  maximise  shared  value  creation.  Recognising  the  critical  role  of  
sustainability in shaping risks and opportunities for our business, we identify our material matters by shortlisting key 
issues across the ESG spectrum. These matters are prioritised based on their significance to our stakeholders and their 
impact on our business.
In FY2025, we conducted a validation exercise to reaffirm the relevance of our material matters. This review confirmed 
that while many identified issues remain pertinent, we have made some adjustments to our material matters to better 
reflect  evolving  stakeholder  expectations  and  industry  trends.  The  updated  list  of  material  matters  will  serve  as  the  
foundation for our reporting, communications, and disclosures for our Sustainability Statement.
An enhanced assessment is scheduled for FY2027, during which we will transition from a single materiality approach to 
a double materiality framework. This shift aims to align our practices with the latest sustainability trends and reporting 
standards. The comprehensive assessment will consider both inside-out and outside-in perspectives, enabling us to 
identify a list of ESG material issues that are most pertinent to KIP REIT and our stakeholders. 
Stakeholder Engagement and Materiality Assessment Process
Our stakeholder engagement and materiality assessment exercise in FY2025 involved a structured approach to ensure 
alignment with our business strategy and the evolving sustainability landscape. The process consisted of the following 
key steps: 
          Review of Stakeholder Groups and Sustainability Matters
We began by reviewing our existing list of stakeholder groups and material matters to assess their alignment with 
KIP  REIT’s  strategic  objectives  and  current  market  trends.  This  review  included  an  evaluation  against  relevant  
sustainability reporting frameworks and industry standards to ensure comprehensive coverage of key issues.

TENANT ENGAGEMENT 
KIP  REIT  places  a  high  priority  on  regular  tenant  engagement  as  a  key  strategy  for  continuous  improvement  and  
tenant satisfaction. The REIT Manager, Property Manager and Service Provider are dedicated to maintaining ongoing 
communication  with  tenants  to  understand  their  expectations  and  foster  an  environment  conducive  to  growth  and

•  Email  is  also  available  as  an  alternative,  ensuring  tenants  have  multiple  channels  to  contact  the  
management if needed.
• For prompt contact and swift communication, tenants can also connect with KIP REIT on social media 
anytime.
Through active engagement with tenants, KIP REIT can identify areas for improvement and implement changes that 
enhance tenant experience and satisfaction. 
This  proactive  approach  not  only  addresses  immediate  concerns  but  also  fosters  a  collaborative  atmosphere  where  
tenant feedback directly contributes to operational improvements.
COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT WITH TENANTS
KIP  REIT  is  deeply  committed  to  community  engagement  initiatives.  These  efforts  are  designed  to  strengthen  
relationships with tenants and the broader community. For example, KIP REIT organises various events and activities at 
the Managed Assets to build a sense of community and belonging, thereby creating a positive and supportive business 
environment. This initiative highlights KIP REIT's commitment to giving back to the community and celebrating national 
milestones together.
Through these robust tenant and community engagement strategies, KIP REIT aims to create a dynamic and responsive 
business atmosphere that supports tenant needs and drives economic performance. By continuously fostering strong 
tenant  relationships  and  participating  in  meaningful  community  activities,  KIP  REIT  ensures  that  its  approach  to  
economic performance is both holistic and sustainable.
INCREASING RENTAL POTENTIAL
KIP  REIT  adopts  a  comprehensive  and  strategic  approach  to  increase  rental  potential  through  meticulous  tenant  
selection, footfall management system, and robust Asset Enhancement Initiatives (“AEIs”). This dual focus is pivotal to 
ensuring sustainable income growth and long-term asset value.
This process is designed to maximise property occupancy rates and secure a stable stream of rental income. By choosing

tenants who align with our goals and the specific needs of our properties, KIP REIT not only stabilises rental income 
but also enhances the overall value of its assets. This strategic approach ensures that our properties are occupied by 
high-quality tenants who contribute positively to the property environment and align with our long-term objectives.

competitive, relevant, and in demand. We invested RM4.2 million in targeted AEIs to keep our assets aligned with market

In  FY2025,  KIP  REIT  successfully  completed  the  AEI  at  KIPMall  Senawang,  marking  a  key  milestone  in  enhancing

system  that  integrates  work  order  management,  preventive  maintenance,  asset  tracking,  vendor  operations,  and  
contract management into a single digital platform.

GOVERNANCE
CORPORATE GOVERNANCE 
OVERVIEW STATEMENT
At  KIP  REIT,  we  uphold  the  highest  standards  of  
corporate governance, integrity, and ethical conduct 
in   fund   management.   Our   governance   practices   
are    built    on    transparency,    accountability,    and    
responsibility   responsibilities,   which   are   essential   
to  sustaining  long-term  value  for  unitholders  and  
stakeholders. 
The Board of Directors maintains rigorous oversight 
of  our  comprehensive  anti-corruption  framework.  
This includes regular review and approval of policies 
that  address  all  forms  of  corruption  –  from  bribery  
(encompassing  facilitation  payments  and  kickbacks)  
to  money  laundering  risks  in  tenant  transactions,  
conflicts  of  interest,  and  potential  obstruction  of  
justice   such   as   document   falsification.   Through   
quarterly  reports,  the  Board  of  Directors  assesses  
the  effectiveness  of  our  anti-bribery  and  corruption  
management system. 
To  preserve  institutional  integrity,  we  also  regularly  
assesses   KIP   REIT’s   governance   frameworks   and   
business     practices.     This     includes     monitoring     
developments  in  political,  economic,  technological,  
and     socio-environmental     domains,     such     as     
digital    transformation,    cybersecurity,    workplace    
culture  shifts,  and  climate  change.  These  ongoing  
evaluations enable us to remain agile and resilient in 
a rapidly evolving landscape.

The     Compliance     Officer     supports     effective     
governance policy implementation. He is responsible 
for  proposing  policy  enhancements  for  the  Board  
of  Directors’  review  and  approval,  ensuring  that  KIP  
REIT’s  governance  system  remains  robust,  current,  
and  capable  of  fostering  an  ethical  and  transparent  
culture. The outsourced Internal Audit function also 
plays a critical role by assessing the effectiveness of 
internal controls and risk management processes.
We also extend our governance expectations across 
the  entire  value  chain.  All  third-party  engagements,  
including suppliers, contractors, and tenants, will be 
bound  by  our  Suppliers’  Code  of  Conduct,  which  
includes  anti-bribery  and  compliance  requirements.  
These  standards  will  be  reinforced  through  routine  
due  diligence,  annual  declarations,  and  compliance  
reviews.
WHY IS THIS TOPIC MATERIAL TO US?
Corporate     governance     and     anti-corruption     
management    is    fundamental    to    KIP    REIT’s    
sustainable growth and competitive positioning in 
the  REIT  sector.  Strong  governance  frameworks  
directly  impact  our  ability  to  attract  and  retain  
quality tenants, secure favourable financing terms, 
and maintain investor confidence.
Under  Section  17A  of  the  MACC  Act  2009,  KIP  
REIT  faces  direct  legal  liability  for  corruption  by  
associated   persons,   making   robust   anti-bribery   
controls not just best practice but a legal necessity. 
Governance    failures    could    trigger    regulatory    
investigations,   disrupt   property   operations,   and   
compromise  tenant  relationships  that  form  the  
foundation of our revenue streams.
From   an   investment   perspective,   institutional   
investors    and    lenders    increasingly    integrate    
governance quality into their risk assessments and 
funding  decisions.  Superior  governance  standards  
enhance our access to capital markets and reduce 
borrowing costs. 
WHAT IS OUR COMMITMENT?
KIP  REIT  maintains  an  absolute  zero-tolerance  
stance    against    bribery,    fraud,    and    unethical

Anti-Bribery Management System
Our  Anti-Bribery  Management  System  (“ABMS”)  establishes  a  robust  foundation  for  ethical  business  practices  
through comprehensive policies, procedures, and control measures. We have developed this integrated approach to 
effectively  mitigate  corruption  risks  and  promptly  address  any  instances  of  non-compliance  or  unethical  behaviour.  
Our commitment to the highest standards of corporate governance is demonstrated by embedding anti-corruption 
and anti-financial crime principles into our daily operations. At the core of our ABMS is a comprehensive Anti-Bribery 
and  Anti-Corruption  (“ABAC”)  program  that  aligns  with  national  anti-corruption  efforts  and  adopts  a  zero-tolerance  
approach against all forms of corruption. This systematic approach serves as our primary defence mechanism against 
corporate liability under subsection 17A (5) of the MACC Act 2009.
Training and Awareness
Our approach to building an ethical culture centres on continuous training and awareness programs designed to reach 
all stakeholders. We conduct comprehensive mandatory ABAC training sessions for all employees annually, reinforcing 
our zero-tolerance stance against bribery and corruption. Our consolidated training curriculum covers detailed ABAC 
policies and procedures, real-world case studies illustrating various forms of bribery and corruption, practical scenarios, 
and legal implications and regulatory requirements. 
To ensure thorough comprehension, we administer post-training assessments requiring a minimum passing score of at 
least 50%, which not only evaluates understanding but also reinforces the critical importance of adhering to our anti-
corruption policies. We also provide specialised anti-bribery and corruption training to our Board of Directors, ensuring 
our  leadership  remains  well-informed  about  current  anti-corruption  practices  and  policies,  enabling  them  to  set  a  
strong ethical example and effectively guide the organisation in upholding the highest standards. 
Extending  beyond  internal  stakeholders,  our  ABMS  encompasses  all  business  intermediaries  through  systematic  
distribution of our Anti-Bribery and Corruption (“ABC”) Policy and ancillary anti-corruption policies. This ensures clear 
communication  of  our  ethical  expectations  and  compliance  requirements  throughout  our  business  relationships,  
fostering a culture of integrity across our entire network of partners and vendors.

Enterprise Risk Management Framework
Our  Enterprise  Risk  Management  (“ERM”)  Framework  incorporates  specialised  
risk   assessments   and   procedures   designed   to   address   corruption   risks,   
particularly  those  associated  with  intermediaries  and  high-risk  operations.  We  
conduct thorough corruption risk assessments covering all elements and types 
of  corruption,  including  bribery,  comprehensive  anti-corruption  risk  mapping,  
regular  evaluation  of  operational,  geographical,  and  transactional  risks,  and  
third-party  and  intermediary  risk  profiling.  For  operations  assessed  as  “high  
risk”, we implement enhanced procedures addressing all elements and types of 
corruption  including  bribery,  comprehensive  anti-corruption  measures  tailored  
to specific risk profiles, enhanced due diligence requirements, and strengthened 
monitoring and oversight mechanisms.
In  alignment  with  Bursa  Malaysia’s  Common  Indicator  C1(b),  we  also  systematically  assess  corruption-related  risks  
across  all  our  operations.  We  measure  our  comprehensive  coverage  through  tracking  the  percentage  of  operations  
assessed  for  corruption-related  risks,  ensuring  that  each  location  undergoes  thorough  evaluation  for  all  forms  of  
corruption including bribery, facilitation payments, fraud, extortion, collusion, and money laundering. This systematic 
approach  enables  us  to  maintain  complete  visibility  of  corruption  risks  across  our  operational  footprint  while  
demonstrating compliance with the MACC Act 2009 and supporting our sustainability reporting requirements.

Whistleblowing Channel
Central to our integrity framework is our confidential whistleblowing channel, which serves as a crucial element for 
maintaining transparency and empowering stakeholders to report concerns without fear of retaliation. Our approach 
ensures  confidential  and  anonymous  reporting  capabilities,  protection  against  retaliation  for  good-faith  reporting,  
multiple  reporting  channels  to  accommodate  different  comfort  levels,  and  prompt  and  thorough  investigation  
procedures.   We   maintain   comprehensive   procedures   for   addressing   reported   concerns,   including   immediate   
assessment and triage of reports, independent investigation processes, appropriate disciplinary and corrective actions, 
and regular reporting to Senior Management and the Board.
We  recognise  that  effective  anti-corruption  efforts  require  engagement  across  all  levels  through  regular  communication  
of  our  zero-tolerance  policy,  clear  guidelines  and  expectations  for  all  stakeholders,  accessible  resources  and  guidance  
materials, and open dialogue channels for questions and clarifications. This comprehensive ABMS represents our unwavering 
commitment to ethical business practices and serves as our primary mechanism for preventing, detecting, and addressing 
corruption in all its forms. Through this integrated approach, we maintain our position as a responsible corporate citizen 
while protecting our organization, stakeholders, and the broader community from the harmful effects of corruption.
WHAT IS THE VALUE WE CREATED IN FY2025?
Five  years  after  establishing  our  foundational  governance  policies,  KIP  REIT  undertook  a  comprehensive  
review  and  enhancement  of  our  entire  corporate  governance  framework  in  FY2025.  This  strategic  refresh  
strengthened our ethical business practices through four key policy upgrades.
Completely Revised Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy: We overhauled our cornerstone policy to explicitly 
codify  our  zero-tolerance  commitment  while  introducing  stronger  compliance  mechanisms  and  clearer  
enforcement protocols.
Newly  Strengthened  Gift,  Hospitality,  Donations  and  Similar  Benefits  Policy:  The  enhanced  policy  
establishes a “No Gift” principle with specific monetary thresholds and mandatory pre-approval requirements. 
This  eliminates  ambiguity  around  acceptable  exchanges  and  provides  unambiguous  guidance  across  all  
business relationships.
Separate but Complementary Conflict of Interest Policies: We implemented distinct policies for Directors and 
employees. Directors must formally declare interests annually and quarterly with clear governance protocols, 
while  employees  face  immediate  disclosure  requirements  for  any  personal  relationships  affecting  business  
decisions. This bifurcated approach ensures appropriate governance at both strategic and operational levels.
Substantially  Improved  Whistleblowing  Policy:  We  enhanced  our  reporting  ecosystem  with  stronger

confidentiality protections, complete anonymity options, explicit anti-retaliation guarantees, and standardised 
investigation protocols. These improvements foster an organisational culture where ethical concerns can be 
raised without fear of reprisal.
Together, these policy enhancements demonstrate KIP REIT’s proactive commitment to maintaining industry-
leading governance standards in the REIT sector.
